claim: Flask.create_url_adapter(request) is in app.py around line 425 and binds the url_map to the request.
If TRUSTED_HOSTS is set, it is copied to request.trusted_hosts.
With TRUSTED_HOSTS set, request.host is recomputed with werkzeug.wsgi.get_host(environ, trusted_hosts).
get_host raises a SecurityError, a 400, for an untrusted host.
This host check happens inside RequestContext.__init__, so any HTTPException there is stored as request.routing_exception and raised later in dispatch_request.
With host_matching, SERVER_NAME is not passed to Werkzeug, so the real Host header is used for matching.
Without subdomain_matching, create_url_adapter forces the subdomain to url_map.default_subdomain or "".
create_url_adapter returns url_map.bind_to_environ(environ, server_name=..., subdomain=...).
With no request, create_url_adapter can only build an adapter if SERVER_NAME is set.
With no request, create_url_adapter uses APPLICATION_ROOT as the script name and PREFERRED_URL_SCHEME.
With no request and no SERVER_NAME, create_url_adapter returns None.
RequestContext.match_request() calls url_adapter.match(return_rule=True).
When matching fails, Werkzeug raises NotFound, MethodNotAllowed or RequestRedirect (for a missing trailing slash).
Flask stores the matching exception on request.routing_exception instead of raising it.
Matching runs after the session is opened, so custom URL converters can use the session.
The routing exception is raised in dispatch_request() by raise_routing_exception().
before_request functions and URL value preprocessors still run for unmatched URLs.
For an unmatched URL, request.endpoint is None and request.blueprints is [].
In debug mode, a RequestRedirect that is not 307/308 on a non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS request is replaced by debughelpers.FormDataRoutingRedirect.
FormDataRoutingRedirect is an AssertionError that explains the browser would drop the form body.
The app reads request.blueprints, which is wrappers.Request.blueprints.
For an endpoint parent.child.view, request.blueprints is ["parent.child", "parent"], innermost first.
request.blueprints is computed by the cached helpers._split_blueprint_path.
URL value preprocessors run in preprocess_request in the order app, outermost blueprint, innermost blueprint, in registration order within a scope.
before_request functions run in preprocess_request in the order app, outermost blueprint, innermost blueprint, in registration order within a scope.
The first non-None return from a before_request function short-circuits.
after_this_request functions run in process_response from a per-request list on the RequestContext, in registration order.
after_request functions run in process_response in the order innermost blueprint, outermost blueprint, app, in reverse registration order within a scope.
teardown_request functions run in do_teardown_request in the order innermost blueprint, outermost blueprint, app, in reverse registration order.
teardown_appcontext functions run in do_teardown_appcontext, app only, in reverse registration order.
Template context processors run in update_template_context in the order app, outermost blueprint, innermost blueprint, in registration order.
Error handlers are looked up by _find_error_handler from the innermost blueprint to the app, then by MRO.

handle_user_exception(e) is called from full_dispatch_request for any Exception raised by preprocess_request or dispatch_request.
If e is a BadRequestKeyError and debug or TRAP_BAD_REQUEST_ERRORS is on, handle_user_exception sets e.show_exception = True.
If e is an HTTPException and trap_http_exception(e) is false, handle_user_exception passes it to handle_http_exception(e).
Otherwise handle_user_exception looks up a handler with _find_error_handler(e, request.blueprints) and re-raises if there is none.
handle_http_exception(e) returns e unchanged when e.code is None (proxy exceptions).
handle_http_exception(e) returns e unchanged when e is a RoutingException such as RequestRedirect.
Otherwise handle_http_exception calls the registered handler, if there is one, and returns the exception itself if there is not.
Werkzeug's HTTPException is a WSGI app, so make_response turns it into an error page.
trap_http_exception(e) returns true if TRAP_HTTP_EXCEPTIONS is set.
If TRAP_BAD_REQUEST_ERRORS is None and the app is in debug mode, trap_http_exception also traps BadRequestKeyError.
If TRAP_BAD_REQUEST_ERRORS is true, trap_http_exception traps every BadRequest.
A trapped HTTP exception is handled like an ordinary exception, so it reaches the debugger when it is not handled.
handle_exception(e) is called from wsgi_app for anything that escaped full_dispatch_request.
handle_exception sends the got_request_exception signal.
handle_exception computes propagate = PROPAGATE_EXCEPTIONS, which defaults to testing or debug.
If propagate is true, handle_exception re-raises.
Otherwise handle_exception calls log_exception(exc_info), which calls app.logger.error("Exception on /path [GET]").
Otherwise handle_exception wraps the error as InternalServerError(original_exception=e).
handle_exception runs a 500 / InternalServerError handler if one exists.
handle_exception calls finalize_request(server_error, from_error_handler=True).
With from_error_handler=True, failures during response processing are logged and ignored instead of raised.
App._find_error_handler(e, blueprints) is in sansio/app.py around line 823.
Handlers are stored as error_handler_spec[scope][code][exc_class].
The code key is the HTTP status for HTTPException subclasses and None otherwise.
register_error_handler(404, f) maps 404 to werkzeug.exceptions.NotFound using default_exceptions.
Registering a handler for the base HTTPException stores it under code None, because HTTPException.code is None.
_find_error_handler iterates codes (e.code, None), then scopes (innermost blueprint to app), then the exception's MRO from most specific class.
Error handler precedence is: blueprint handler for the code, then app handler for the code, then blueprint handler for the class, then app handler for the class.
A request to an unmatched URL has no blueprints, so a blueprint's 404 handler never fires for URLs that did not match one of its routes.
Blueprint.app_errorhandler or an app handler should be used for unmatched URLs.
errorhandler refuses exception instances, non-Exception classes and unknown integer codes.
Every user callback is called as self.ensure_sync(func)(...).
Signal receivers are called through _async_wrapper.
Flask.ensure_sync returns plain functions unchanged and wraps coroutine functions with async_to_sync.
The async_to_sync method imports asgiref.sync.async_to_sync.
If asgiref is missing, it raises RuntimeError("Install Flask with the 'async' extra...").
Each async view runs in its own event loop inside a normal WSGI worker.
docs/async-await.rst explains when to use Quart instead.
Subclasses can override ensure_sync or async_to_sync to change the async behavior.
globals.py defines two contextvars.ContextVar objects and werkzeug.local.LocalProxy objects that read through them.
_cv_app is a ContextVar named "flask.app_ctx".
app_ctx = LocalProxy(_cv_app) is the AppContext itself.
current_app = LocalProxy(_cv_app, "app") is AppContext.app.
g = LocalProxy(_cv_app, "g") is AppContext.g.
_cv_request is a ContextVar named "flask.request_ctx".
request_ctx = LocalProxy(_cv_request) is the RequestContext itself.
request = LocalProxy(_cv_request, "request") is RequestContext.request.
session = LocalProxy(_cv_request, "session") is RequestContext.session.
Each proxy forwards attribute access to the object that is current in the active contextvars context.
With no context active, proxy access raises RuntimeError with the "Working outside of application context" or "Working outside of request context" message.
A proxy is falsy when unbound.
Flask's own code writes `if current_app:` or `if request:` to check whether a context is active, for example in helpers.redirect, helpers.abort, json.dumps and wrappers.Request.max_content_length.
current_app._get_current_object() returns the real object behind a proxy.
Flask uses request_ctx.flashes, request_ctx.url_adapter and request_ctx._get_current_object() in process_response.
AppContext.__init__(app) stores app.
AppContext.__init__ builds url_adapter = app.create_url_adapter(None), which is None unless SERVER_NAME is set.
AppContext.__init__ creates g = app.app_ctx_globals_class().
AppContext.__init__ starts an empty token list.
AppContext.push() calls _cv_app.set(self), keeping the token, then sends appcontext_pushed.
AppContext.pop(exc) calls app.do_teardown_appcontext(exc) if this is the last outstanding push of this object.
AppContext.pop always resets the ContextVar.
AppContext.pop raises AssertionError("Popped wrong app context") when contexts were popped out of order.
AppContext.pop then sends appcontext_popped.
AppContext is a context manager usable as `with app.app_context():`.
An app context is pushed during every request by RequestContext.push.
An app context is pushed during every app.cli command by FlaskGroup.get_command or with_appcontext.
An app context is active in flask shell.
g is a plain namespace object with get, pop, setdefault, in and iteration.
g belongs to the app context, not the request context.
In a normal request a fresh app context is pushed, so g lasts one request.
In examples/tutorial/flaskr/db.py, get_db() caches the connection on g.
In examples/tutorial/flaskr/db.py, close_db is registered with app.teardown_appcontext.
The class of g can be swapped with Flask.app_ctx_globals_class.
RequestContext.__init__(app, environ, request=None, session=None) builds the Request with app.request_class(environ).
RequestContext.__init__ sets request.json_module = app.json.
RequestContext.__init__ creates the URL adapter and stores any HTTPException as routing_exception.
RequestContext.__init__ sets flashes = None.
RequestContext.__init__ sets session, usually None at this point.
RequestContext.__init__ sets _after_request_functions = [].
RequestContext.push() creates and pushes app.app_context() if no app context is active or the active one belongs to a different app, and remembers it so it can pop it later.
Otherwise RequestContext.push() reuses the active app context.
RequestContext.push() then calls _cv_request.set(self).
RequestContext.push() opens the session via session_interface.open_session, falling back to make_null_session, only if self.session is None.
The self.session is None check means pushing again, as stream_with_context does, does not reload the session.
RequestContext.push() then calls match_request().
RequestContext.pop(exc) runs app.do_teardown_request(exc) and request.close() on the last outstanding push.
RequestContext.pop resets the ContextVar.
RequestContext.pop clears environ["werkzeug.request"] to break a reference cycle.
RequestContext.pop pops the app context it pushed, which runs the app-context teardowns, and checks the order.
RequestContext.copy() returns a new RequestContext that shares the same request and the current session.
RequestContext.copy() is used by copy_current_request_context.
Both context classes keep a list of tokens, so the same context object can be pushed more than once.
Teardown runs only when the final pop happens.
has_request_context() and has_app_context() in ctx.py check the ContextVars.
after_this_request(f) adds f to the current RequestContext._after_request_functions.
after_this_request functions run before the regular after_request functions.
copy_current_request_context(f) copies the request context at decoration time and pushes the copy around each call.
copy_current_request_context is meant for greenlets.
copy_current_request_context is not safe across threads unless access to the request object is synchronized.
stream_with_context(gen) in helpers.py wraps a generator so the request context is pushed while it runs.
stream_with_context primes the generator with next() while the view is still running, which pushes the context a second time.
Because of the second push, when wsgi_app pops it is not the final pop, so teardown is deferred until the stream is exhausted.
stream_template() applies stream_with_context automatically when a request is active.
app.test_request_context(...) builds an environ with testing.EnvironBuilder and returns a RequestContext that can be pushed.
A blueprint has the same decorator API as the app, inherited from Scaffold.
A blueprint records most operations as deferred callables and replays them against an app when it is registered.
Blueprint.add_url_rule(...) checks that the endpoint and view function name contain no ".".
Blueprint.add_url_rule calls self.record(lambda s: s.add_url_rule(...)).
Routes are not added to bp.view_functions.
Hooks such as bp.before_request go into the blueprint's own None-scoped dicts inherited from Scaffold and are merged at registration.

The app_* variants before_app_request, after_app_request, teardown_app_request, app_context_processor, app_errorhandler, app_url_value_preprocessor, app_url_defaults and app_template_filter/test/global register app-wide hooks using record_once.
record(func) appends to deferred_functions.
record_once(func) wraps the function so it runs only when state.first_registration is true.
bp.endpoint(name), from Scaffold, writes into bp.view_functions directly.
bp.endpoint entries are merged into app.view_functions without a blueprint prefix, as tests/test_blueprints.py::test_endpoint_decorator shows.
Blueprint.register is in sansio/blueprints.py around line 273.
app.register_blueprint(bp, **options) calls bp.register(app, options).
register works out the registered name as f"{name_prefix}.{options.get('name', bp.name)}".lstrip(".").
Nested blueprints get dotted names such as parent.child.
register raises ValueError if the name is already in app.blueprints.
To register the same blueprint twice, name= must be passed.
register records app.blueprints[name] = self.
register sets _got_registered_once = True, which locks further setup on the blueprint.
register builds a BlueprintSetupState with make_setup_state.
BlueprintSetupState works out the effective url_prefix, subdomain and url_defaults, with option values overriding blueprint attributes.
BlueprintSetupState.add_url_rule joins the prefix onto the rule, sets the subdomain, merges the defaults and registers the endpoint as "{name_prefix}.{name}.{endpoint}".lstrip(".") on the app.
register adds the blueprint's static route if it has a static_folder, with endpoint <name>.static.
register calls _merge_blueprint_funcs(app, name) on the first registration of this blueprint object or of this name.

_merge_blueprint_funcs copies the blueprint's error handlers, view_functions, before/after/teardown functions, URL defaults, URL value preprocessors and template context processors into the app's dicts, re-keyed from None to name.
register runs every deferred function with the state, which is where routes are actually added.
If cli_group is the sentinel default, bp.cli becomes a subgroup named after the blueprint (flask <bpname> <cmd>).
If cli_group is None, the blueprint's commands are merged directly into app.cli.
If cli_group is a string, it names the group.
bp.register_blueprint(child) only queues the child in bp._blueprints.
register recursively registers nested blueprints, joining url_prefix and subdomain with the parent's and passing name_prefix=name.
After registration the app holds everything, and at request time the blueprint objects are only consulted for templates (jinja_loader) and static files.
request.blueprint and request.blueprints are derived from the matched endpoint's dotted prefix in wrappers.py.
url_for(".view") inside a blueprint request resolves to "<current blueprint>.view" in Flask.url_for.
Blueprint templates have lower priority than app templates.
Blueprints are searched for templates in registration order.
A blueprint's static files are only reachable if it has a url_prefix or a distinct static_url_path.
Otherwise the app's /static route takes precedence over the blueprint's static route.
flask.url_for(endpoint, **values) in helpers.py calls current_app.url_for(...).
Flask.url_for is in app.py around line 1003.
In a request, url_for uses the request context's url_adapter.
In a request, a leading "." in the endpoint is resolved against the current blueprint, or stripped if there is none.
In a request, _external defaults to False unless _scheme is given.
Outside a request, url_for uses the app context's url_adapter, or builds one if called directly on the app with no context.
Outside a request, url_for needs SERVER_NAME, otherwise it raises RuntimeError("Unable to build URLs outside an active request without 'SERVER_NAME' configured...").
Outside a request, _external defaults to True.
Passing _scheme with _external=False raises ValueError.
inject_url_defaults(endpoint, values) runs the url_defaults functions for the app, then for each blueprint in the endpoint's dotted path.
inject_url_defaults parses the endpoint string instead of using request.blueprints, so it also works outside a request.
url_for calls url_adapter.build(endpoint, values, method=_method, url_scheme=_scheme, force_external=_external).
Values that are not part of the rule become query string arguments.
A BuildError goes to handle_url_build_error, which tries each function in app.url_build_error_handlers and re-raises if none returns a value.
_anchor is quoted and appended as #anchor.
url_for is also a Jinja global, the bound app.url_for.
Config is a dict subclass with a root_path that relative filenames are resolved against.
Config.from_object(obj_or_import_string) copies uppercase attributes from a module or class using dir(obj).
Config.from_object does not work with a dict.
Config.from_pyfile(filename, silent=False) execs a Python file into a fresh module object and then calls from_object.
With silent=True, from_pyfile ignores ENOENT, EISDIR and ENOTDIR.
Config.from_envvar(name, silent=False) calls from_pyfile(os.environ[name]), with a helpful error if the variable is unset.
Config.from_file(filename, load, silent=False, text=True) opens a file, passes it to load, then calls from_mapping.
Config.from_mapping(mapping=None, **kwargs) is like update but only for uppercase keys.
Config.from_prefixed_env(prefix="FLASK", loads=json.loads) reads FLASK_* env vars in sorted order, strips the prefix and tries json.loads on each value, keeping the string if that fails.
In from_prefixed_env, "__" in a key sets a nested dict entry, for example FLASK_SQLALCHEMY__ECHO.
Config.get_namespace(prefix, lowercase=True, trim_namespace=True) returns the subset of keys starting with prefix.
ConfigAttribute is a descriptor that forwards an attribute to a config key, with an optional converter on read.
App uses ConfigAttribute for testing (TESTING), secret_key (SECRET_KEY) and permanent_session_lifetime (PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME).
For permanent_session_lifetime, an int becomes a timedelta.
debug is a real property that reads and writes config["DEBUG"].
The debug setter also updates jinja_env.auto_reload when TEMPLATES_AUTO_RELOAD is None.
Flask.default_config is in app.py around line 178.
DEBUG defaults to None and is set from FLASK_DEBUG in make_config.
TESTING defaults to False.
PROPAGATE_EXCEPTIONS defaults to None, meaning testing or debug, and is read by Flask.handle_exception.
SECRET_KEY defaults to None.
SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS defaults to None and is read by SecureCookieSessionInterface.get_signing_serializer for key rotation.
PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME defaults to 31 days.
USE_X_SENDFILE defaults to False and is read by helpers._prepare_send_file_kwargs.
TRUSTED_HOSTS defaults to None and is read by Flask.create_url_adapter.
SERVER_NAME defaults to None and is read by create_url_adapter, Flask.run (default host/port) and EnvironBuilder.
APPLICATION_ROOT defaults to "/".
APPLICATION_ROOT is used for URL building outside requests, session cookie path fallback and EnvironBuilder.
SESSION_COOKIE_NAME defaults to "session".
SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN defaults to None.
SESSION_COOKIE_PATH defaults to None.
SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY defaults to True.
SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE defaults to False.
SESSION_COOKIE_PARTITIONED defaults to False.
SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE defaults to None.
The SESSION_COOKIE_* keys are read by SessionInterface.get_cookie_*.
SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST defaults to True and is read by SessionInterface.should_set_cookie.
MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH defaults to None and is read by Request.max_content_length.
MAX_FORM_MEMORY_SIZE defaults to 500_000 and is read by Request.max_form_memory_size.
MAX_FORM_PARTS defaults to 1_000 and is read by Request.max_form_parts.
SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT defaults to None and is read by get_send_file_max_age on both app and blueprint.
TRAP_BAD_REQUEST_ERRORS defaults to None and is read by trap_http_exception and handle_user_exception.
TRAP_HTTP_EXCEPTIONS defaults to False and is read by trap_http_exception.
EXPLAIN_TEMPLATE_LOADING defaults to False and is read by DispatchingJinjaLoader.get_source.
PREFERRED_URL_SCHEME defaults to "http".
PREFERRED_URL_SCHEME is used for URL building outside requests and by EnvironBuilder.
TEMPLATES_AUTO_RELOAD defaults to None, meaning follow debug, and is read by create_jinja_environment and the debug setter.
MAX_COOKIE_SIZE defaults to 4093 and is read by Response.max_cookie_size.
PROVIDE_AUTOMATIC_OPTIONS defaults to True and is read by App.add_url_rule.
DEBUG affects error propagation, trapping, debug redirects, JSON indentation, Jinja auto-reload, logger level and debug helpers.
Debug mode is read from the environment variable FLASK_DEBUG when the config is created.
The CLI's --debug flag works by setting os.environ["FLASK_DEBUG"] in cli._set_debug before the app is imported, so factories see it.
ScriptInfo.load_app then sets app.debug = get_debug_flag() again through the property.
flask.Request extends werkzeug.wrappers.Request.
flask.Request has url_rule, view_args and routing_exception, set during matching.
flask.Request has endpoint, blueprint and blueprints properties derived from url_rule.endpoint.
flask.Request has max_content_length, max_form_memory_size and max_form_parts properties.
Each of these properties returns a per-request override if one was set, then the app config if an app context is active, then Werkzeug's default.
flask.Request has json_module, which is flask.json by default and replaced with app.json per request.
request.get_json() uses the app's JSON provider.
In debug mode, Request._load_form_data patches request.files, if the request is not multipart/form-data and has no files, so that a KeyError raises DebugFilesKeyError explaining the missing enctype.
Request.on_json_loading_failed re-raises a bare BadRequest outside debug mode.
flask.Response extends Werkzeug's Response.
flask.Response has default_mimetype = "text/html".
flask.Response has json_module = flask.json.
flask.Response has autocorrect_location_header = False.
flask.Response has a max_cookie_size read from config.
Setting Flask.request_class and Flask.response_class makes Flask use custom classes.
JSONProvider in json/provider.py is the per-app interface with dumps, loads, dump, load and response.
JSONProvider holds a weakref.proxy to the app.
Subclasses of JSONProvider must implement at least dumps and loads.
DefaultJSONProvider uses the stdlib json module with default=_default, ensure_ascii=True and sort_keys=True.
DefaultJSONProvider._default serializes date and datetime as HTTP dates (RFC 822).
DefaultJSONProvider._default serializes Decimal and UUID as str.
DefaultJSONProvider._default serializes dataclasses with dataclasses.asdict.
DefaultJSONProvider._default serializes objects with __html__.
DefaultJSONProvider.response() pretty-prints with indent=2 when compact is False, or None in debug mode.
Otherwise DefaultJSONProvider.response() uses compact separators.
DefaultJSONProvider.response() always adds a trailing newline and sets mimetype to application/json.
app.json is created from Flask.json_provider_class in App.__init__.
flask.json.dumps, loads, dump and load in json/__init__.py delegate to current_app.json when an app context is active and fall back to the stdlib otherwise.
jsonify(*args, **kwargs) always requires an app context and calls current_app.json.response.
A view that returns a dict or list goes through app.json.response via make_response.
The Jinja |tojson filter is wired to app.json.dumps through jinja_env.policies["json.dumps_function"] in create_jinja_environment.
TaggedJSONSerializer in json/tag.py is a separate, lossless format for session data.
TaggedJSONSerializer wraps values JSON cannot represent as single-key dicts with a tag key.
The tag key " t" is for tuple.
The tag key " b" is for bytes (base64).
The tag key " m" is for Markup.
The tag key " u" is for UUID.
The tag key " d" is for datetime.
The tag key " di" is for dicts that happen to collide with a tag key.
TaggedJSONSerializer.register(TagClass, index=...) adds custom tags.
Session cookies use TaggedJSONSerializer, not app.json.
Flask.session_interface is a class attribute, SecureCookieSessionInterface() by default.
A SessionInterface must implement open_session(app, request) and save_session(app, session, response).
open_session is called in RequestContext.push after the context is set and before URL matching.
open_session returns a session object, or None, in which case make_null_session is used.
save_session is called at the end of Flask.process_response, after all after_request functions.
save_session is skipped when is_null_session(session) is true.
SessionInterface provides cookie-parameter getters that read the SESSION_COOKIE_* config.
SessionInterface.get_expiration_time returns now plus the lifetime if session.permanent, else None, meaning a browser-session cookie.
SessionInterface.should_set_cookie returns modified or (permanent and SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST).
SessionMixin adds the permanent property, backed by the "_permanent" key.
SessionMixin adds the new, modified and accessed flags.
SecureCookieSessionInterface.get_signing_serializer(app) returns None if there is no secret_key.

Otherwise get_signing_serializer returns an ItsDangerous URLSafeTimedSerializer with keys=[*SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS, SECRET_KEY], salt="cookie-session", serializer=TaggedJSONSerializer() and signer_kwargs with key_derivation hmac and digest_method sha1.
The current key goes last because ItsDangerous signs with the last key and accepts all of them for verification.
SHA-1 is looked up lazily (_lazy_sha1) so FIPS builds can import Flask.
SecureCookieSessionInterface.open_session returns None with no secret key, which produces a NullSession.
With a missing cookie, open_session returns an empty SecureCookieSession.
Otherwise open_session calls s.loads(cookie, max_age=PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME).
On BadSignature, which includes expiry, open_session returns an empty session instead of raising.
save_session adds a Vary: Cookie header if the session was accessed.
If the session is empty and was modified, save_session deletes the cookie.
If the session is empty, save_session writes nothing.
If should_set_cookie is false, save_session writes nothing.
Otherwise save_session sets the signed cookie with the configured attributes.
SecureCookieSession is a Werkzeug CallbackDict.
Any top-level mutation of SecureCookieSession sets modified and accessed, and reads set accessed.
Changing a nested mutable value such as session["cart"].append(x) is not detected.
NullSession allows reads but raises RuntimeError("The session is unavailable because no secret key was set...") on any write.
flash(message, category) in helpers.py appends (category, message) to session["_flashes"].
flash reassigns the list so external-storage sessions see the change.
flash sends message_flashed.
get_flashed_messages(with_categories, category_filter) pops _flashes from the session the first time it is called in a request.
get_flashed_messages caches the result on request_ctx.flashes, so later calls in the same request return the same messages.
app.jinja_env is a cached_property on App that calls Flask.create_jinja_environment() the first time it is accessed.
create_jinja_environment starts from app.jinja_options.
create_jinja_environment sets autoescape=select_jinja_autoescape.
select_jinja_autoescape is true for .html, .htm, .xml, .xhtml and .svg, and for string templates.
create_jinja_environment sets auto_reload from TEMPLATES_AUTO_RELOAD, falling back to debug.
create_jinja_environment creates app.jinja_environment(app, **options), which is Flask's Environment subclass.
Flask's Environment loader defaults to app.create_global_jinja_loader().
create_jinja_environment adds globals url_for, get_flashed_messages, config, and the request, session and g proxies.
The request, session and g proxies are added as globals so imported templates and macros can see them too.
create_jinja_environment sets the json.dumps_function policy to app.json.dumps.
DispatchingJinjaLoader looks up a template name with the app's own jinja_loader first.
The app's jinja_loader is a FileSystemLoader on root_path/template_folder, and template_folder defaults to templates.
DispatchingJinjaLoader then tries each blueprint's loader in registration order, and the first match wins.
Blueprint templates therefore never override app templates, and two blueprints using the same template name conflict.
With EXPLAIN_TEMPLATE_LOADING=True, _get_source_explained tries every loader and logs a report through debughelpers.explain_template_loading_attempts.
render_template(name_or_list, **context) gets the template with jinja_env.get_or_select_template.
A list passed to render_template means the first template that exists.
render_template calls _render.
_render calls app.update_template_context(context).
update_template_context runs the context processors for the app, then for the blueprints from outermost to innermost.
Explicitly passed values win over processor values.
_render sends before_render_template, renders, and sends template_rendered.
render_template_string does the same with jinja_env.from_string.
stream_template(_string) uses template.generate().
stream_template(_string) wraps the generator with stream_with_context if a request is active.
For streamed templates, template_rendered is sent once generation finishes.
_default_template_ctx_processor is pre-registered in every Scaffold under scope None.
_default_template_ctx_processor injects g, request and session as the real objects, not proxies.
app.template_filter, template_test and template_global (and the add_* versions) write directly into jinja_env.
Using app.template_filter and similar creates the Jinja environment, so jinja_options must be set before.
The blueprint app_template_* versions write into jinja_env at registration time.
get_template_attribute(template, name) in helpers.py gives Python code access to a macro or variable exported by a template.
The app's static route and each blueprint's static route call send_static_file(filename).
send_static_file calls send_from_directory(static_folder, filename, max_age=self.get_send_file_max_age(filename)).
Flask and Blueprint each have their own copy of get_send_file_max_age and send_static_file, and the docstrings note they are duplicates.
helpers.send_file and send_from_directory are thin wrappers around werkzeug.utils.send_file and send_from_directory.
_prepare_send_file_kwargs adds environ=request.environ, use_x_sendfile=USE_X_SENDFILE, response_class=app.response_class and _root_path=app.root_path.
_prepare_send_file_kwargs defaults max_age to current_app.get_send_file_max_age.
send_from_directory uses safe_join, so it is safe for paths that come from users.
send_file is not safe for paths that come from users.
app.open_resource(path, mode="rb", encoding=None) opens files under root_path, read-only.
app.open_instance_resource(...) opens files under instance_path and allows writes.
Blueprint.open_resource opens relative to the blueprint's root.
The default encoding is None for Flask.open_resource.
The default encoding is "utf-8" for Blueprint.open_resource and open_instance_resource.
The [project.scripts] entry flask = "flask.cli:main" calls cli.main().
python -m flask (__main__.py) calls cli.main().
cli is a module-level FlaskGroup(name="flask").
AppGroup subclasses click.Group.
AppGroup.command() wraps callbacks in with_appcontext, and with_appcontext=False opts out.
AppGroup.group() defaults to AppGroup.
app.cli and bp.cli are AppGroups.
FlaskGroup subclasses AppGroup and is the flask command itself.
FlaskGroup adds the eager options -e/--env-file, -A/--app and --debug/--no-debug, plus --version.
FlaskGroup sets auto_envvar_prefix="FLASK".
The auto_envvar_prefix makes FLASK_APP, FLASK_DEBUG, FLASK_ENV_FILE and FLASK_RUN_PORT work as environment variables.
FlaskGroup adds the built-in run, shell and routes commands.
FlaskGroup loads plugin commands from the flask.commands entry point group via _load_plugin_commands.
FlaskGroup.get_command(ctx, name) first looks up built-in and plugin commands, which work even if the app fails to load.
FlaskGroup.get_command then loads the app with ScriptInfo.load_app(), pushes an app context with ctx.with_resource(app.app_context()) and looks the name up in app.cli.
FlaskGroup.list_commands merges the built-in and app commands and prints load errors without crashing.
FlaskGroup.make_context sets os.environ["FLASK_RUN_FROM_CLI"] = "true".
FLASK_RUN_FROM_CLI=true turns a stray app.run() into a no-op.
FlaskGroup.make_context creates the ScriptInfo object.
FlaskGroup.parse_args processes --env-file and --app early when only --help or no arguments are given, so that the app's commands show up in the help text.
ScriptInfo holds app_import_path, an optional create_app callable, set_debug_flag and load_dotenv_defaults.
ScriptInfo.load_app() caches the app.
ScriptInfo.load_app search order is create_app() if given, then --app/FLASK_APP parsed as module_or_path[:name], then wsgi.py, then app.py in the current directory.
The --app value is split on a colon that is not followed by a path separator, so Windows drive letters work.
prepare_import(path) turns a file path into a module name by walking up through __init__.py packages.
prepare_import puts the package's parent directory at the front of sys.path.
locate_app(module, name) imports the module.
locate_app tells apart "module not found" and "ImportError raised inside the module" by checking the traceback depth.
find_best_app(module) tries app or application first.
find_best_app then tries a single Flask instance among the module's globals, raising an error if there are several.
find_best_app then tries a create_app or make_app factory called with no arguments.
find_app_by_string(module, "create_app('dev', debug=True)") parses the string with ast.
find_app_by_string allows only a plain name or a call whose arguments are literals, using ast.literal_eval.
_called_with_wrong_args tells apart a TypeError caused by calling the factory with the wrong arguments from a TypeError raised inside the factory.
The run command has options --host, --port, --cert, --reload/--debugger, --with-threads, --extra-files and --exclude-patterns.
--cert accepts a file, adhoc, or an import path to an SSLContext, validated by CertParamType and _validate_key.
--reload and --debugger both default to debug.
--extra-files and --exclude-patterns use SeparatedPathType, split on os.pathsep.
The run command calls werkzeug.run_simple.
If the app fails to import while running under the reloader, run prints the error and serves a WSGI app that re-raises it, so the reloader keeps watching files.
The shell command uses code.interact with app.make_shell_context().
make_shell_context provides app, g and any @app.shell_context_processor results.
The shell command honors PYTHONSTARTUP and sets up readline completion.
The routes command prints endpoint, methods, domain and rule.
The routes command hides HEAD and OPTIONS unless --all-methods is given.
The routes command prints the domain column only if any rule has a host or subdomain.
The routes command sorts by --sort endpoint|methods|domain|rule|match.
The routes sort option match keeps the url_map iteration order.
load_dotenv(path=None, load_defaults=True) is a no-op without python-dotenv, apart from printing a tip if .env files exist.
Dotenv precedence from highest to lowest is: variables already in the environment, the -e file, .env, then .flaskenv.
The dotenv files are found by searching upward from the current directory.
Flask.run() also calls load_dotenv() unless FLASK_SKIP_DOTENV disables it, via helpers.get_load_dotenv.
Flask.run() returns immediately if FLASK_RUN_FROM_CLI is set.
Otherwise Flask.run() loads dotenv.
Flask.run() applies FLASK_DEBUG and then the debug argument.
Flask.run() takes default host and port from SERVER_NAME, falling back to 127.0.0.1:5000.
Flask.run() defaults use_reloader and use_debugger to debug.
Flask.run() defaults threaded to True.
Flask.run() calls werkzeug.serving.run_simple.
Flask defines ten Blinker signals in a private Namespace.
Each Flask signal is sent with the app object as sender and _async_wrapper=app.ensure_sync.
request_started is sent from Flask.full_dispatch_request before preprocess_request, with no extra kwargs.
request_finished is sent from Flask.finalize_request after process_response, with the kwarg response.
got_request_exception is sent from Flask.handle_exception, only for exceptions that reach it, with the kwarg exception.
request_tearing_down is sent from Flask.do_teardown_request with the kwarg exc.
appcontext_tearing_down is sent from Flask.do_teardown_appcontext with the kwarg exc.
appcontext_pushed is sent from AppContext.push with no extra kwargs.
appcontext_popped is sent from AppContext.pop with no extra kwargs.
before_render_template is sent from templating._render and _stream with the kwargs template and context.
template_rendered is sent from templating._render and _stream, after generation, with the kwargs template and context.
message_flashed is sent from helpers.flash with the kwargs message and category.
tests/test_signals.py uses template_rendered.connect(receiver, app) to capture the context a template was rendered with.
View requires overriding dispatch_request(**view_args).
View.as_view(name, *args, **kwargs) returns a plain view function.
By default View.as_view creates a new instance for each request.
With init_every_request = False, one instance is reused.
The function returned by as_view gets view_class, __name__, __doc__, __module__, methods and provide_automatic_options attributes, which add_url_rule reads.
The class attribute decorators is applied to the generated function.
Decorating the View class itself does nothing for routing.
MethodView.__init_subclass__ collects the HTTP method names the class defines (get, post, ...) and those of its bases into methods.
MethodView.dispatch_request calls the method matching request.method, falling back from HEAD to get.
View and MethodView use current_app.ensure_sync, so async def get() works.
app.test_client() returns a FlaskClient, or app.test_client_class, a subclass of Werkzeug's Client.
FlaskClient's default environ_base has REMOTE_ADDR=127.0.0.1 and a Werkzeug user agent.
FlaskClient requests are built with Flask's EnvironBuilder.
EnvironBuilder takes base_url defaults from SERVER_NAME (or localhost), APPLICATION_ROOT and PREFERRED_URL_SCHEME.
EnvironBuilder accepts subdomain and url_scheme.
EnvironBuilder serializes json= with app.json.
Using the client as `with client:` sets preserve_context = True.
With preserve_context, the client injects environ["werkzeug.debug.preserve_context"], which Flask.wsgi_app calls in its finally block to hand over the app and request contexts.
The client pushes the preserved contexts again after the response, so request and session can be inspected until the with block ends.
Contexts preserved from an earlier request are popped at the start of the next request.
session_transaction() opens the session through a temporary test request context, yields it for editing, then saves it into the client's cookie jar.
response.json_module is set to app.json, so response.get_json() and response.json use the app's provider.
app.test_cli_runner() returns a FlaskCliRunner(CliRunner).
FlaskCliRunner.invoke() defaults to app.cli and passes a ScriptInfo(create_app=lambda: self.app).
The built-in commands run, shell and routes live on FlaskGroup, not on app.cli.
app.test_request_context(...) uses EnvironBuilder to produce a RequestContext without dispatching.

tests/conftest.py has fixtures app_ctx, req_ctx, client and test_apps.
The test_apps fixture adds tests/test_apps to sys.path and cleans up imported modules afterwards.

tests/conftest.py has an autouse leak_detector fixture that fails any test leaving a request context pushed.
app.logger is a cached_property that calls logging.create_logger(app).
The logger is logging.getLogger(app.name).
The logger is set to DEBUG level in debug mode if no level is set yet.
If no handler in the logger hierarchy handles its effective level (has_level_handler), the logger gets flask.logging.default_handler.
default_handler is a StreamHandler writing to wsgi_errors_stream.
wsgi_errors_stream is environ["wsgi.errors"] during a request and sys.stderr otherwise.
app.name is the import name.
For __main__, app.name is the running script's file stem.
debughelpers.py holds FormDataRoutingRedirect, DebugFilesKeyError / attach_enctype_error_multidict, and explain_template_loading_attempts.

session_interface defaults to SecureCookieSessionInterface().
json_provider_class defaults to DefaultJSONProvider.

test_client_class and test_cli_runner_class default to None, which resolves to FlaskClient and FlaskCliRunner.

Flask has no special extension API.
The extension convention is an init_app(app) function or method that stores state in app.extensions["name"].
The extension convention registers hooks such as app.teardown_appcontext(...), CLI commands via app.cli.add_command and config defaults via app.config.setdefault.
Extensions read current_app at runtime instead of keeping an app reference, so one extension instance can serve several apps.
docs/extensiondev.rst describes the extension convention.

claim: Process / app object state lives on the Flask instance: config, url_map, view_functions, hook registries, blueprints, extensions, jinja_env, json and logger.
App context state lives in AppContext: g and url_adapter (if SERVER_NAME).
Request context state lives in RequestContext: request, session, flashes, url_adapter and _after_request_functions.
Session data persists across requests in a signed cookie on the client side.
Adding routes, hooks or blueprints after the app has handled a request raises AssertionError via setupmethod.
Changing a blueprint after registering it raises AssertionError.
before_request runs even for 404s, because routing errors are stored and raised in dispatch_request after preprocess_request.
An app @errorhandler(404) beats a blueprint @errorhandler(HTTPException).
If an app context for the same app is already active, such as client.get() inside `with app.app_context():`, RequestContext.push reuses it.
When the app context is reused, g and the app-context teardowns outlive the single request.
With TESTING=True the test client raises the view's exception instead of returning a 500.
With no secret key by default, the session is a NullSession whose reads work and writes raise.
Expired or tampered session cookies quietly become an empty session.
save_session runs in process_response, so session changes made inside a streaming generator are not persisted.
stream_with_context delays teardown until the generator finishes.
A generator without stream_with_context cannot use request once the view returns.
The Jinja environment is created lazily and only once, so jinja_options changes after the first app.jinja_env access have no effect.
jinja_options changes after any template_filter/template_global registration have no effect.
url_for outside a request needs SERVER_NAME and produces absolute URLs by default.
app.run() is ignored under flask run because of FLASK_RUN_FROM_CLI.
test_cli_runner().invoke(args=["routes"]) fails because it invokes app.cli, which does not contain the built-in commands.
To test built-in commands, flask.cli.cli or a FlaskGroup must be passed explicitly to invoke.
bp.endpoint("name") is not prefixed with the blueprint name, unlike bp.route.
HEAD comes from Werkzeug whenever GET is allowed.
OPTIONS is added by Flask unless PROVIDE_AUTOMATIC_OPTIONS=False or the view opts out.

The project uses uv with dependency groups ([dependency-groups] in pyproject.toml) and a lock file (uv.lock).
[tool.uv] default-groups = ["dev", "pre-commit", "tests", "typing"].
`uv sync` creates .venv and installs Flask (editable) plus the dev, pre-commit, tests and typing groups.
`uv run pytest` runs the full test suite, with testpaths = ["tests"].
`uv run pre-commit install` installs hooks for ruff, ruff-format, uv-lock and whitespace.
The build backend is flit_core.
The package is src/flask.
[tool.tox] in pyproject.toml uses tox-uv with the uv-venv-lock-runner.
The tox envs py3.13, py3.12, py3.11, py3.10 and pypy3.11 run pytest on locked latest deps.
The tox env tests-min runs pytest with the minimum supported versions of Werkzeug, Jinja, Click, etc.
The tox env tests-dev runs pytest against the main branches of the Pallets dependencies.
The tox env style runs pre-commit run --all-files.
The tox env typing runs mypy (strict) and pyright over src and tests/type_check.
The tox env docs runs sphinx-build -W, with warnings as errors.
The tox env docs-auto is a live-reloading docs server.
CI in .github/workflows/tests.yaml runs `uv run --locked tox run -e <env>`.
CI runs on Linux, plus Windows and macOS on 3.13, PyPy, and the min/dev dependency versions.
A separate CI job runs typing.
pytest config has filterwarnings = ["error"], so any warning fails the test.
mypy runs in strict mode.
tests/type_check/*.py are not executed but are type-checked to make sure public decorators keep their signatures.
Ruff lint rules are B, E, F, I, UP and W.
The isort rule in ruff uses force-single-line imports, which is why every import in the source is on its own line.
